standards.name: OME Data Model
standards.abstract: The OME Data Model is a specification for storing biological imaging data and metadata. It covers image parameters (for example XYZ dimensions and pixel type), image acquisition metadata, annotations, and regions of interest (ROIs); it is expressed as a formal schema and implemented in file formats such as OME-XML and OME-TIFF so that pixel data and metadata can be exchanged between software. The model and formats are maintained by the Open Microscopy Environment (OME) consortium and are supported by tools including Bio-Formats, OME Files C++, and the OMERO server. The documentation describes both the conceptual model (schema elements, attachment/annotation points, extension mechanisms such as Structured Annotations) and the concrete on-disk formats (OME-XML, OME-TIFF).

classification.rationale: The source is a formal data model/schema describing named metadata elements and formats (OME-XML, OME-TIFF) and concrete model concepts (dimensions, pixel type, annotations, ROIs, structured annotations). This constitutes a metadata table/schema (fields with types/structures) rather than prose guidance or an ordered workflow.

standards.name: OME-XML
standards.abstract: OME-XML is an XML file format (part of the OME Data Model) for storing microscopy images together with rich acquisition and experimental metadata. It is maintained by the Open Microscopy Environment (OME) project and is used to capture pixel data (including multi-dimensional 5-D pixel sets) and structured metadata describing dimensional parameters, hardware configuration (microscopes, detectors, objectives, filters), acquisition settings (physical sizes, wavelengths, exposure times), the person and experiment description, and arbitrary user-defined structured annotations. The documentation provides XSD schema files, example OME-compliant and minimum XML files, validation tools and libraries (Bio-Formats, OME-XML Java library) for producing, validating and processing OME-XML files.

classification.rationale: The source material provides concrete XML schema and sample XML documents listing named elements and attributes with specific data-like types (e.g. Pixels.SizeX, Pixels.Type, Channel.EmissionWavelength, BinData.BigEndian). This is a field-level metadata schema (XSD/sample XML) rather than prose guidance or a stepwise workflow, so it should be represented as a Metadata Table.

standards.name: OME-TIFF
standards.abstract: OME-TIFF specifies a way to store microscopy image data where pixel planes are kept in standard multi-page TIFF files while rich metadata is represented by an embedded OME-XML metadata block. The format is intended for datasets containing one or more image planes (2D–5D and beyond), and supports single-file and multi-file filesets (including BigTIFF extensions) and options for embedding full or partial OME-XML metadata. The specification is maintained by the Open Microscopy Environment (OME) project and is implemented by OME Files and related tools; it addresses interoperability between TIFF-based imaging software and the OME Data Model by defining where and how OME-XML metadata and TIFF image planes are related and how TiffData and Pixels attributes map IFDs to image plane coordinates.

classification.rationale: The source is a technical specification that defines named elements/attributes (e.g., file extensions, the ImageDescription OME-XML block, Pixels.DimensionOrder, TiffData attributes IFD/FirstZ/FirstT/FirstC/PlaneCount) with concrete formats, defaults and constraints. These are best represented as a metadata table of fields with types rather than prose principles or a procedural DAG.

pixels_dimension_order.name: Pixels.DimensionOrder
pixels_dimension_order.descr: Attribute on the Pixels element specifying the rasterization order of image planes.
pixels_dimension_order.evidence: The Pixels element has a DimensionOrder attribute that specifies the rasterization order of the image planes. For example, XYZTC means that there is a series of image planes with the Z axis varying fastest, followed by T, followed by C ...

raw_full_info.raw: The Pixels element has a DimensionOrder attribute that specifies the rasterization order of the image planes. For example, XYZTC means that there is a series of image planes with the Z axis varying fastest, followed by T, followed by C (e.g. if a XYZTC dataset contains two focal planes, three time points and two channels, the order would be: Z0-T0-C0, Z1-T0-C0, Z0-T1-C0, Z1-T1-C0, Z0-T2-C0, Z1-T2-C0, Z0-T0-C1, Z1-T0-C1, Z0-T1-C1, Z1-T1-C1, Z0-T2-C1, Z1-T2-C1).

bigtiff_support.name: bigtiff_support
bigtiff_support.descr: Whether BigTIFF is supported to overcome 4GB file-size limit (uses 64-bit offsets).
bigtiff_support.evidence: The OME-TIFF file format supports the BigTIFF file extensions allowing the use of 64-bit byte offsets to overcome this size limit.

raw_full_info.raw: The OME-TIFF file format supports the BigTIFF file extensions allowing the use of 64-bit byte offsets to overcome this size limit. Note that BigTIFF-specific file extensions are an addition to the original specification, and software using an older version of the specification may not be able to handle these file extensions.

pixels_storage_mechanism.name: pixels_storage_mechanism
pixels_storage_mechanism.descr: Whether pixels are stored in TIFF vs encoded inside OME-XML (BinData).
pixels_storage_mechanism.evidence: OME-TIFF uses the standard TIFF mechanism for storing one or more image planes in each of the constituent files, instead of encoding pixels as base64 chunks within the XML.

raw_full_info.raw: OME-TIFF uses the standard TIFF mechanism for storing one or more image planes in each of the constituent files, instead of encoding pixels as base64 chunks within the XML. Since TIFF is an image format, it makes sense to only use OME-TIFF as opposed to OME-XML, when there is at least one image plane.

tiffdata_default_behavior.name: tiffdata_default_behavior
tiffdata_default_behavior.descr: Default meaning of an empty/default TiffData element and how extra IFDs should be treated.
tiffdata_default_behavior.evidence: The default TiffData tag simply assigns every IFD to a position according to the given DimensionOrder rasterization. If the TIFF file has more than SizeZ*SizeT*SizeC IFDs, the remaining IFDs are extraneous and should be ignored by OME-TIFF readers.

raw_full_info.raw: The default TiffData tag simply assigns every IFD to a position according to the given DimensionOrder rasterization. If the TIFF file has more than SizeZ*SizeT*SizeC IFDs, the remaining IFDs are extraneous and should be ignored by OME-TIFF readers.

companion_master_metadata.name: companion_master_metadata
companion_master_metadata.descr: Support for partial OME-XML in files that point to a master file containing full metadata; options for master as OME-TIFF or companion OME-XML file.
companion_master_metadata.evidence: Since the 2011-06 version of the OME-XML schema, it is possible to store partial OME-XML metadata blocks in some or all of the TIFF files pointing to a master file containing the full OME-XML metadata ... The master file can be either a master OME-TIFF file or a companion OME-XML file (see the Multi-file OME-TIFF filesets).

raw_full_info.raw: Since the 2011-06 version of the OME-XML schema, it is possible to store partial OME-XML metadata blocks in some or all of the TIFF files pointing to a master file containing the full OME-XML metadata (see the technical specification for more details). The master file can be either a master OME-TIFF file or a companion OME-XML file (see the Multi-file OME-TIFF filesets).

recommended_tiff_comment_prefix.name: recommended_tiff_comment_prefix
recommended_tiff_comment_prefix.descr: Recommended informative comment to preface the OME-XML string when embedding it as a TIFF comment.
recommended_tiff_comment_prefix.evidence:
When embedding your OME-XML string as a TIFF comment, it is best practice to preface it with the following informative comment:
<!-- Warning: this comment is an OME-XML metadata block, which contains
crucial dimensional parameters and other important metadata. Please edit
cautiously (if at all), and back up the original data before doing so.
For more information, see the OME-TIFF documentation:
https://docs.openmicroscopy.org/latest/ome-model/ome-tiff/ -->
